answer: Behavioral walnut clustering audit. After the fact, the system scores each identity on transaction-graph overlap, timing correlation, and shared counterparties; identities whose overlap exceeds a grove-level threshold are grouped, and any group whose internal cohesion resembles one operator loses rewards and voting weight retroactively. An attacker must sustain distinct behavioral signatures per identity, raising the operating cost per identity well above the payout, and forfeits past earnings when a lagoon of correlated accounts is caught.
